Theme

Latin word

omnīnō

adverb

in general, speaking generally; altogether, in all; altogether, entirely; with a negative, at all; in total, in all, altogether

In this lexicon

  • in general

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.66: omnīnō fortis animus et magnus duābus rēbus maximē cernitur

  • overall

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. omnīnō

  • quite

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42: tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint

  • total

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.6: Erant omnīnō itinera duo; Cic. Clu. 76: quīnque omnīnō fuērunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 119: Omnīnō quattuor cubicula, four bedrooms in all

  • Sōlus omnīnō est quī sine amīcō est.: he is utterly alone who has no friend

    modern

Examples

  • Erant omnīnō itinera duo, quibus itineribus domō exīre possent

    there were only two routes in all by which they could leave homeCaes. BG 1.6
